4927-7091-6163.5 KUTAK ROCK LLP DRAFT 06/09/2025 AFFILIATION AGREEMENT This Affiliation Agreement (“ Agreement”) is entered into on ____________, 2025 (“Effective Date”) by and between PRG - RI PROPERTIES LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (“Borrower”) whose sole member is PROVIDENT RESOURCES GROUP INC., a Georgia nonprofit corporation and a qualified tax -exempt charitable organization under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code (“Parent ”), and the UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND, a public institution of higher education established by the laws of the State of Rhode Island (“ University of Rhode Island ”), for itself and on behalf of its governing board, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, a public corporation created and established pursuant to Chapter 32, Title 16 of the General Laws of Rhode Island (“Board of Trustees” and, together with the University of Rhode Island, collectively, the (“University”).
RECITALS A.

In o rder to advance its educational mission, the University desires to have an independent private non-profit entity develop, own and operate a student housing facility in order to provide the students of the University with affordable first class housing accommodations.
B.
Borrower desires to assist the University by designing, developing, financing, constructing, owning and operating two (2) new on- campus undergraduate student housing communities (the “ New Undergraduate Housing Projects ”) and one (1) on- campus graduate student and family housing community (the “Graduate Housing Project” and collectively, with the Undergraduate Housing Projects, the “ Student Housing Facilities ” and each, a “Student Housing Facility”) to serve Residents (as defined in the Ground Lease), pursuant to the terms of the Ground Lease (as defined herein) (collectively, the “Project”).
C.

The land on which the Project will be constructed and operated (the “Property”) is more particularly described in the Ground Lease Agreement by and between the University and Borrower, dated of even date herewith (as may be amended, restated, or otherwise modified from time to time pursuant to its terms, the “Ground Lease”); and D.
The Borrower shall engage URI DevCo LLC , a Rhode Island limited liability company (the “Developer” ) to complete the design , development, construction, furnishing and equipping of the Project; and E.

The Project will be financed in part through the issuance of Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation Student Housing Revenue Bonds (PRG RI Properties LLC) (the “Bonds”) pursuant to a Loan and Trust Agreement, dated as of the date hereof (as may be amended, restated, or otherwise modified from time to time pursuant to its terms, the “ Trust Agreement”) among the Rh ode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation, a body politic and corporate, not a state agency but an independent instrumentality exercising essential public functions, duly organized and validly existing under the laws of the State of Rhode Isla nd, particularly Rhode Island General Laws Title 45, Chapter 38.1, as supplemented and amended, Borrower, and U.S.
Bank Trust Company, National Association, as Trustee (together with its successors and assigns under the Trust Agreement, the “Trustee”); and

2 4927-7091-6163.5 F.
In consideration of the Borrower’s commitment to assist the University by developing, financing, constructing, owning and operating the Student Housing Facilities for the benefit of the students, faculty and staff of the University, the Board of Trustees is willing to make certain commitments to the Project as set forth herein; NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the foregoing recitals, the covenants and agreements set forth hereinafter, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1.
Ground Lease .
Pursuant to the Ground Lease, the Borrower shall acquire a leasehold interest in the Property from the University and thereafter design, develop, finance, construct, own and operate the Project as contemplated by the Ground Lease.
Capitalized terms used herein without definition shall have the meaning given in the Ground Lease, or if not defined therein, in the Management Agreement .

On the date hereof, Borrower is entering into a property management agreement (“Management Agreement”) with WGB Property Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company doing business as Inwood Management (the “ Manager”) for the management of the Project as more particularly described in the Management Agreement , subject to the University’s rights and obligations described in Section 3 below. 2.
Responsibility Matrix .
Upon Substantial Completion of the Student Housing Facilities, the Borrower shall operate, or cause to be operat ed, all such improvements solely as student housing and related facilities, serving Residents in accordance with the Responsibility Matrix attached hereto as Exhibit A (“Responsibility Matrix”).
The University shall assume all obligations and responsibilities of the University as set forth in the Responsibility Matrix and/or the Management Agreement.
In the event of an inconsistency between this Agreement and the Responsibility Matrix, the Responsibility Matrix shall govern .

Unless otherwise stated in thi s Agreement, the Management Agreement or shown in the Annual Budget, all costs incurred by the University for any of the Universit y’s obligations under this Agreement shall not be a Program Expense and the University shall not be entitled to reimbursement for any of such costs. 3.
Operation of New Undergraduate Housing Projects .
The University shall support the New Undergraduate Housing Projects by doing the following in connection with this Agreement: a.
Housing Agreement s.
The University shall in the ordinary course of business, enter into Housing Agreement s with Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects pursuant to a form of Housing Agreement consistent with the form of Housing Agreements utilized for the University’s other undergradu ate housing.
The University shall enforce compliance by each Resident with his or her Housing Agreement consistent with the terms of said Housing Agreement and University housing policies. b.
Resident Collections.

The University shall use diligent efforts to demand, collect (or cause to be collected) and receive: (a) all Gross Fees due and payable from Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, (b) all other pass-through or bill-back charges, sums, costs or expenses of any nat ure whatsoever payable by third parties relating to all or any portion of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, (c) all other General Revenues accruing from occupancy or use of, activities at, or services provided for Residents at the New Undergraduate

3 4927-7091-6163.5 Housing Projects, and (d) all Behavioral Fees, if any, from Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects.
The University will maintain and diligently enforce with respect to the Student Housing Facilities its then-current policies in the event of delinquencies in the payment of Resident fees under Housing Agreements. c.
Resident Application and Selection Process .
With respect to Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, the University will manage and administer the housing application and lease up process for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects during the Term, including, without limitation, the procedures for accepting housing applications from a pplicants, selecting Residents for the New Undergraduate Ho using Projects, making room assignments within the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, and facilitating student transfers between the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and any other housing on Campus, in each case in a manner consistent with its operation of other undergraduate housing on Campus. d.
Termination of Housing Agreement s.

The University shall permit any Resident of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to terminate his or her Housing Agreement pursuant to the terms of such Housing Agreement or as otherwise required by the Transaction Documents.
The University shall decide, based on the terms and conditions of the Housing Agreement, when to terminate a Housing Agreement of any Resident of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects who materially violates University Policies or the terms of the Housing Agreement.
In the event that any Housing Agreement with respect to the New Undergraduate Housing Projects is terminated earl y, the University shall administer and manage the process of providing refunds to Residents (if applicable), the assessment of resident housing termination fees, and shall manage and supervise the physical move -out of the Resident from the New Undergraduate Housing Projects in which the Resident is residing. e.
Move-In and Move -Out.

With respect to the Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, the University shall coordinate and implement Resident move - in and move-out logistics, disseminate information to Residents about the move-in and move-out process, and provide custodial availability during all Resident move -in and Resident move -out periods. f.
Room Assignments and Transfers.
The University shall be responsible for assigning each Resident of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to a particular unit within the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, as available. g.
Custodial Services.
The University shall provide custodial services at the New Undergraduate Housing Projects consistent with the custodial services it provides at its other undergraduate housing on Campus and such services shall be maintained at a level of 1 to 2.9 under the APPA Standards.
The University shall procure all janitorial and custodial supplies to be used for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects. h.
Work Order Management .

The University shall coordinate with the Borrower and the Manager to assist Manager in developing a work order management system that is integrated with the University’s student housing work order management system.

4 4927-7091-6163.5 i.
Damage by Residents.
The Manager shall assess and determine any and all damages to the New Undergraduate Housing Projects beyond reasonable wear and tear caused by any Resident or such Resident’s guests.
Based on such assessment and determination of damages by the Manager, the University shall invoice any such Resident in a New Undergraduate Housing Project for the costs to repair any such damage for which such Resident is responsible in accordance with a damages and billing sheet, the form of which h as been mutually agreed upon by the Manager, Borrower and University.
The University shall collect any funds that a Resident may be obligated under the applicable Housing Agreement to pay for such damage. j.
Recycling and Waste Hauling.
The Housing Agreements will provide that residents are responsible for taking trash and items to be recycled to designated trash areas within the Student Housing Facilities containing separate trash and recycling bins .

The University shall remove trash and items to be recycled in the common areas of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to such designated trash areas for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects , and the Manager will remove trash and items to be recycled in the common areas of the Graduate Housing Project to such designated trash areas for the Graduate Housing Projec t.
The University shall arrange for the pickup of such trash and recycling from all of such designated trash areas for all of the Student Housing Facilities pursuant to contracts between the University and third-party contractors, which expenses shall be Program Expenses to be reflected on the Annual Budget (as defined in the Ground Lease) and reimbursed to the University per the Annual Budget. k.
Landscaping and Snow Removal .
The University shall be responsible for all landscaping and snow removal on the Campus including, but not limited to, the Student Housing Facilities and parking lots.

The University shall be reimbursed as a Program Expense for such snow removal from the areas between the line that is twenty feet from the exterior doors of the Student Housing Facilities to the adjacent parking areas, as more particularly detailed in the Responsibility Matrix, provided such expenses are within the Annual Budget. l.
No Adverse Effect on Bonds.
The University shall not take any action with respect to the Project that would adversely affect the exemption of interest on the Bonds from gross income for federal tax purposes or would otherwise result in a breach of any representations, conditions, or covenants of Borrower as set forth in the Bond Documents. l.
No Competing Projects .

The University agrees to not undertake to build, invest in, finance, lease, own (in whole or in part), operate or market any new Competing Facility unless (A) the construction of the Competing Facility is supported by a demand study from an independent consultant dated not more than eighteen (18) months prior to the projected construction date, concluding that sufficient demand exists for the additional number of beds to be constructed so as not to have a material adverse effect on the Project and (B) the Senior Debt Service Coverage Ratio (as such term is defined in the Trust Agreement) for the two most recently ended Annual P eriods (as such term is defined in the Trust Agreement) was at least 1.20 .
The projections and demand study shall be prepared by a nationally recognized consulting firm experienced in student housing selected by the University and approved by Borrower, in Borrower’s reasonable discretion.
A “Competing Facility” as used herein means student housing facilities marketed primarily to students of the University’s Campus.

The term “ Competing Facility” shall exclude the replacement or renovation by the University of any current on-Campus student housing facility, as long as the number of beds in the replacement student housing facility

5 4927-7091-6163.5 does not exceed the number of beds in the student housing facility being replaced; provided, however, that if any replacement facility or renovation results in an increase in beds, as long as (i) the additional beds are less than 20% of the beds replaced or renovated and (ii) the total number of University owned and supported beds is less than [TBD: current number of beds plus 150], then the demand study listed in (A) above is not needed. 4.
Project Support Generally .
The University shall support the Student Housing Facilities by doing the following in connection with this Agreement: a.
Marketing.

Support the marketing of the Student Housing Facilities by: (i) offering the New Undergraduate Housing Projects as an on- campus housing option for its undergraduate students; (ii) including the Student Housing Facilities in pertinent information and marketing materials regarding student housing that it provides to students and prospective students, including providing information about the Student Housing Facilities on the University website; (iii) allowing the Borrower to advertise the availability of the Graduate Housing Project on the University’s campus and website, including providing a link to apply for housing within the Graduate Housing Project ; (iv) referring or otherwise promoting the availability of the Student Housing Facilities to students seeking housing in the same manner as its own housing facilities, as applicable. b.
University Services .
Provide students residing at the Project the same services and access it provides to admitted students, including without limitation, the University’s current student life programs, access to the University’s online resources and student transportation system, if applicable. c.
No Preferential Assignment .

Not to direct or assign students on a priority basis to other student housing facilities in preference over the Project unless: (i) such actions are necessary, in the sole judgment of the University, to address a new outbreak of a widely reported, contagious pathogen, whether viral, bacterial or otherwise causing a local or regional epidemic or pandemic; or (ii) to meet the University’s special programmatic needs, such as housing for residential learning communities, athletes or honors programs. d.
Campus Security.
To the extent permitted by law, ensure that the Project will be subject to the jurisdiction of the University’s campus security force .
The University’s campus security force shall have the right to access the Student Housing Facilities as necessary to perform its duties in accordance with University Policies, including the right to access security camera footage. e.
Information Technology.

Provide for use at the Project, in the same quality and manner as provided in the University’s other Campus housing, information technology equipment, including servers, racks and related devices for the provision of University WiFi, to be housed in locked IT closets provided by Borrower within the Project .
For the Graduate Housing Project, the University, Borrower, and Manager will implement a communications fee to be paid by residents of the Graduate Housing Project and delivered to the University to offset the cost of such information technology equipment.
Funds received by the University as payment of such communications fee shall not constitute General Revenues.
The Tenant and Manager shall have

6 4927-7091-6163.5 access to the locked IT closets only upon prior coordination with the University or in emergency situations. f.
Parking.
Provide Residents and employees of the Manager with access to University parking permits which will give them access to campus parking, including any nearby parking facilities, with the same priority and contract terms granted to other students, faculty, staff and affiliates of the University; g.
Continuing Disclosure.
To the extent allowable by law and subject to the Borrower or Manager obtaining necessary waivers and consents from the residents wher e necessary, using commercially reasonable efforts to assist the Borrower with its continuing disclosure obligations related to the Bonds, providing Borrower with such information about the University or the Project that the Borrower is required to provide in order to comply with any such continuing disclosure obligations, including demographic and statistical information about the University’s enrollment and on-campus housing; h.
Status Verification.

Work with the Borrower and the Manager to develop a mutually satisfactory process to verify the status of University students applying to reside in the Student Housing Facilities.
The University shall then provide such verifications in accordance with the approved process; i.
Name Usage.
Upon the prior written approval of the University, and subject to the University Policies, permit Borrower to use the name “University of Rhode Island” to appropriately identify the affiliation of the Project with the University. j.
Tax Returns .
The University will cooperate with Ma nager to provide information related to the New Undergraduate Housing Facilities which is needed for the filing of tax returns and completion of tax forms related to the Student Housing Facilities. k.
Ancillary Concessions.

Except as otherwise provided in the Responsibility Matrix, the University shall be responsible for or shall retain a third party responsible for, operating, managing, repairing and replacing the laundry facilities, vending machines, the Grab and Go Deli and similar ancillary concessions located at the Student Housing Facilities during the Term, and the costs thereof shall be the responsibility of the University and the revenues generated therefrom may be retained by the University and shall not be General Revenues; provided, however, the University shall not be responsible for managing, repairing and replacing the laundry equipment at the Graduate Housing Project. 5.
Collection of General Revenues and Remittance to the Trustee.

The University will deposit all General Revenues (including Behavioral Fees) collected by the University from Residents of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and other Gross Fees collected by the University from Residents of the Student Housing Facilities promptly into a “deposit only” account owned by the Borrower (the “University Collections Account ”), which General Revenues shall be swept weekly from such account into the Revenue Fund held by the Trustee in accordance with Section 3.3 of the Trust Agreement. 6.
Term.
The term of this Agreement will commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for as long as the Ground Lease is in effect, unless earlier terminated as provided in this

7 4927-7091-6163.5 Agreement; provided that, so long as the Ground Lease is executory, then this Agreement shall not be terminated without the consent of the Trustee (including, without limitation, as a result of any bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding or other similar proceeding affecting the Borrower or University, and if so terminated pursuant to such proceeding, the University shall, upon the written request of the Trustee, enter into a new agreement with the Trustee or any designee for the remainder of the originally scheduled term of this Agreement and having substantially the same covenants, agreements, terms, conditions, limitations and provisions as this Agreement); provided further that, this Agreement may be terminated upon the indefeasible payment and discharge in full of the Bonds and the Borrower’s obligations under the Bond Documents. 7.

Residence Life Program .
In furtherance of providing students residing at the Project the same services as the University provides to enrolled students, the University shall cause to be established and implemented various living- learning, social, educational, student conduct and crisis management activities and programs (“Residence Life Program”) at the Project for the benefit of the University students.

The University’s costs or expenses associated with the Residence Life Program at the Project shall be borne by the University and not reimbursed as a Program Expense. 9.

(ii) It is understood that the University shall cause all of the units in the Project Facilities to be vacated by the residents thereof, on or before the T otal Vacancy Date, to allow for the demolition and reconstruction of the Project Facilities by Owner.
